channel.title: Israel National News Flashes

item.title: Shabbat Shalom!
item.description:
Arutz Sheva-Israel National News is stopping its round-the-clock news updates at this time in honor of the start of Shabbat in North America, where they are being written now.
Updates will resume Saturday night from Israel, following the conclusion of Shabbat at 17:14 Jerusalem time.
Shabbat Shalom!

item.title: Costa Rica bars anti-Israel UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese from entering country
item.description:
Costa Rica denies entry to anti-Israel UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese, citing an international alert over alleged links to terrorist acts. Israel welcomes move.
(Arutz Sheva-Israel National News' North American desk is keeping you updated until the start of Shabbat in New York. The time posted automatically on all Israel National News articles, however, is Israeli time.)

item.title: Shabbat Shalom from Israel!
item.description:
Arutz Sheva-Israel National News' Israel desk is stopping its round-the-clock news updates at this time in honor of Shabbat. Jerusalem candle lighting time is 15:56 on Friday. Our North American desk will keep you informed until the 16:12 EST candle lighting time in New York.
The updates from Israel will resume Saturday night, following the conclusion of Shabbat at 17:14 in Jerusalem.
Shabbat Shalom!

item.title: Israel’s home prices fall as sales slow and unsold inventory remains high
item.description: November figures show prices down 1.5% from a year earlier, with more than 85,000 new homes awaiting buyers.

item.title: Tzvi Succot explains: This is why the Arabs demand the Education Committee
item.description: Five months after Tzvi Succot pledged to work to close an Arab high school in Jerusalem, police issued a closure order. The school, which operated without a license, was found to have prohibited Palestinian Authority teaching materials.

item.title: Report: Son of senior Hamas official Khalil al-Hayya targeted in Gaza strike
item.description: According to Sky News Arabia, Khalil al-Hayya's son was the target of a strike early this morning in western Gaza City. His fate remains unclear.

item.title: Watch: Terrorist walks among ruins - and is killed
item.description: IDF, Shin Bet, eliminate Hamas and Islamic Jihad terrorists in Khan Yunis and northern Gaza, including three who infiltrated Israel during the October 7 massacre.

item.title: Report: Prosecutors oppose dropping charges in Netanyahu trial
item.description: After judges assessed conviction in Case 4000 as unlikely, prosecutors reportedly favor pursuing Cases 2000 and 4000 and appealing any acquittal; Attorney General is expected to discuss the judges' recommendations.

item.title: IDF: Hezbollah uses fishing boats to spy on Israeli Navy
item.description: Interrogations reveal Hezbollah operatives use civilian fishing boats to photograph, gather intelligence on naval forces, urging Lebanese fishermen to keep their distance.

item.title: Report on Abbas sparks uproar: Katz compares his strategy to that of Hamas leaders
item.description: Defense Minister Israel Katz attacked Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas over reports he will call Hamas a terrorist group, comparing his strategy to Yahya Sinwar's and warning of Muslim Brotherhood infiltration of Israeli power centers.

item.title: Matan Kahana breaks silence: 'Netanyahu is trying to stall and trigger another election'
item.description: Knesset Speaker Matan Kahana accuses Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of trying to stall, trigger another election, while remaining at the helm of the caretaker government.

item.title: Terror attack thwarted in Binyamin, terrorists arrested
item.description: Three terrorists planning imminent attack arrested in village, Duvdevan commandos and paratroopers raid homes, carry out arrests.

item.title: Security leadership divided: Strike Iran without the US?
item.description: Mossad Director Roman Gofman supports independent Israeli strike on Iran if there is no alternative; IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir believes currently no immediate threat, prefers act jointly with US.

item.title: Harish childcare provider arrested over suspected toddler abuse
item.description: Police arrested childcare provider from Umm al-Fahm on suspicion of assaulting toddlers at a Harish preschool.

item.title: Ben Gvir and Smotrich reject Abbas’ Hamas declaration: ‘A political maneuver’
item.description: Ministers Itamar Ben Gvir, Bezalel Smotrich, accuse Ra'am chairman Mansour Abbas of seeking power through deception after reports say he'll label Hamas a terrorist organization.

item.title: The price of uncertainty
item.description: Last Friday, Wall Street looked as if it had finally decided that the great AI boom had run out of road. What followed over the next few trading sessions was a masterclass in how quickly human certainty can reverse itself - and a remarkable parallel to one of the Torah's most mysterious episodes.

item.title: IDF eliminates October 7 terrorist who took part in hostage ‘ceremony’
item.description: Yousef Ayidi, who infiltrated Israel on October 7 and participated in the staged handover of three hostages, named among four Hamas terrorists eliminated in Gaza.

item.title: Welcome back to Britain, Rabbi Dee
item.description: His reception has ironically proved his warning to British Jews to be all too correct. On his trip to the Britain where he was born and which was once his home, Rabbi Dee has been forced to speak in clandestine meetings held by Jews in their own homes. Like in the USSR of old. Op-ed.

item.title: Religiously observant in 2026, or how to save Islam from itself
item.description: Naming religion as a cause of Jihadi violence is not an attack on Islamic faith, but the only way to save it. A voice from Australia as Hanukkah and the anniversary of the Bondi Beach Massacre approach..
